name: AussieWeb Local Search
best_for: Australian businesses wanting a genuinely free listing with a documented verification process behind it.
limitations: Most entries were not created by the businesses they describe. The operator states: “Most of the details on this site were found on publicly available internet sites.” An entry here is therefore not evidence that a business chose to be listed.

name: Herold
best_for: Austrian businesses wanting a free entry in the country’s best-known directory.
limitations: The operator markets “Besseres Google-Ranking” as a benefit. That is a marketing claim and is NOT adopted here; no ranking outcome is asserted.

name: Bulgarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry
YellowPages.ca
best_for: Canadian businesses wanting a listing in the country’s best-known commercial directory.
limitations: The free listing is REQUESTED, not published. The operator’s wording is “REQUEST YOUR FREE ONLINE LISTING”, and what the free tier contains is not enumerated on that page.

name: n49
best_for: Canadian businesses wanting a free listing on a platform that documents its tiers and prices openly.
limitations: The free listing is explicitly NOT verified. The operator lists “Not Verified” as a characteristic of the free tier, and sells verification as a paid upgrade, so a free entry here carries no verification of any kind.

name: Firmy.cz
best_for: Czech businesses wanting the single most visible domestic local citation, tied to the country’s own search engine.
limitations: Creating an entry is confirmed; claiming an existing third-party entry is not documented, so no claim flow is asserted.

name: Zlaté stránky
best_for: Czech businesses wanting a second domestic citation alongside the Seznam catalogue.
limitations: Whether a basic entry is free is NOT documented. The operator promotes paid highlighting, but the existence of a paid option establishes nothing about the basic entry, so cost is recorded as unknown.

name: Das Telefonbuch
best_for: German businesses wanting a free entry in the country’s long-established telephone directory.
limitations: Creating an entry is confirmed; claiming an existing one is not documented, so no claim flow is asserted.

name: Das Örtliche
best_for: German businesses wanting one free submission that reaches three established national directories.
limitations: A submission is not confined to this directory. The same form publishes to Das Telefonbuch and Gelbe Seiten, which is convenient but removes the choice of appearing in only one.

name: Gelbe Seiten
best_for: German local businesses wanting a free listing in a long-established national directory.
limitations: An entry is a REQUEST, not a publication. The operator states that submitted data “werden an den für Ihre Region zuständigen Gelbe Seiten Verlag geschickt. Dort erfolgt eine redaktionelle Prüfung.”

name: 11880.com
best_for: German local businesses wanting a free entry on a directory whose profiles carry customer ratings.
limitations: Ratings exist, but whether a business owner can respond to them is NOT documented, so no owner-response capability is asserted.

name: wlw (Wer liefert was)
best_for: German-speaking B2B suppliers wanting to be found by professional buyers in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
limitations: Whether a basic profile is free is NOT documented. A premium profile is offered on request, but the existence of a paid tier does not establish that the basic tier is free, so cost is recorded as unknown.

name: Capterra
best_for: SaaS vendors selling to SMB and mid-market buyers
limitations: Vendor listing pricing is not disclosed on the homepage

name: Clutch
limitations: Listing pricing is not disclosed publicly

name: Crunchbase
limitations: Most analytical depth sits behind a paid plan

name: G2
best_for: B2B software vendors who want a moderated, reviewed product profile
limitations: No accessible official page states what a vendor listing costs

name: Google Business Profile
best_for: Businesses with a physical location or face-to-face customer contact
limitations: Changes take effect only after the profile has been verified

name: Product Hunt
best_for: New software products seeking a launch moment
limitations: Promoted placements exist, so ranking is not purely organic

name: Trustpilot
best_for: Consumer-facing businesses collecting public reviews
limitations: Open review model is susceptible to review manipulation

name: Yelp for Business
limitations: Review recommendation software filters some reviews

name: AlternativeTo
limitations: Rankings reflect community opinion rather than structured testing

name: Atlassian Marketplace
limitations: Listing pricing not disclosed publicly

name: DesignRush
limitations: Listing pricing not disclosed

name: Docker Hub
limitations: Pull-rate limits apply to unauthenticated users

name: Foursquare Places
limitations: Primarily a data product rather than a self-service listing directory

name: GetApp
best_for: SaaS vendors comparing against category peers
limitations: Vendor listing pricing not disclosed

name: GitHub Marketplace
limitations: No rating or review mechanism visible on the index

name: HubSpot App Marketplace
limitations: Review functionality not evident from the marketplace index

name: Hugging Face
best_for: Teams publishing open models or datasets
limitations: Publishing is unmoderated, so quality varies widely

name: JetBrains Marketplace
limitations: Only the marketplace name could be confirmed from the landing page; other fields are unverified

name: Open Collective
best_for: Open-source projects needing transparent finances
limitations: Pricing for creating a collective is not stated on the homepage

name: OpenCorporates
limitations: Records are only as current as the upstream register

name: PR Newswire
best_for: Regulated or material announcements needing documented wire distribution
limitations: Paid distribution only

name: PeerSpot
limitations: Vendor listing pricing not disclosed

name: ProvenExpert
best_for: Businesses in the German-speaking market wanting a review profile with an openly priced upgrade path.
limitations: The free tier is capped. The operator lists a limited number of displayed reviews and a single active survey per month, so a free profile is a sample of the product rather than a full one.

name: Python Package Index (PyPI)
limitations: No editorial review of package quality

name: Salesforce AppExchange (AgentExchange)
limitations: Storefront is mid-rebrand, so naming is currently ambiguous

name: Shopify App Store
limitations: Restricted to the Shopify ecosystem

name: Software Advice
best_for: SaaS vendors wanting advisor-driven lead flow
limitations: Buyer-side advice is monetised through vendor referrals

name: SourceForge
limitations: Reputation was damaged by past bundled-installer practices under previous ownership

name: Visual Studio Marketplace
limitations: Ratings and review functionality not confirmed from the landing page

name: Wellfound
limitations: Oriented to hiring rather than general company discovery

name: WooCommerce extensions
limitations: Review functionality not confirmed

name: WordPress Plugin Directory
limitations: Plugins must be GPL-compatible

name: npm
best_for: Distributing a JavaScript or TypeScript library to Node and browser projects
limitations: No pre-publication review process is documented

name: Add-ons for Firefox
limitations: Submission cost not stated on the landing page

name: Chambers and Partners
best_for: Firms competing for recognised international legal rankings
limitations: Heavy annual submission burden

name: Drupal Modules
limitations: Restricted to the Drupal ecosystem

name: F-Droid
limitations: Excludes proprietary applications by design

name: Flathub
limitations: Review system not confirmed from the storefront

name: Hex
limitations: Private packages require a paid organisation tier

name: Joomla! Extensions Directory
limitations: Smaller ecosystem than WordPress or Drupal

name: Kaggle Datasets
best_for: Organisations releasing open datasets
limitations: Review system not confirmed from the catalogue page

name: LibHunt
limitations: Rankings derive from social mentions rather than assessment

name: Maven Central
limitations: Publishing requires namespace verification, which is slower than peer registries

name: NuGet Gallery
limitations: Vendor-operated rather than foundation-governed

name: Ollama Library
best_for: Model publishers targeting local-first deployment
limitations: Operated by a single commercial entity

name: Packagist.org
limitations: Private packages require a paid separate product

name: RubyGems.org
limitations: Publishing cost is not stated on the homepage

name: SaaSHub
limitations: Very large catalogue with correspondingly light curation

name: Slashdot Software Directory
limitations: Shares its review corpus with SourceForge, so listings overlap heavily

name: Snap Store
limitations: Backend is single-vendor and not open source

name: Swift Package Index
best_for: Publishing a Swift package so Swift developers can discover it
limitations: No quality threshold is applied to packages that meet the technical requirements

name: The Legal 500
best_for: Law firms seeking recognised practice-area rankings
limitations: Submission is an annual research cycle rather than a listing

name: crates.io
limitations: No quality review of published crates

name: pub.dev
limitations: Publishing cost not stated on the homepage

name: Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce
Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks
PagineGialle
best_for: VAT-registered Italian businesses wanting a free national directory profile.
limitations: An Italian VAT number is required. The registration page carries the condition “*Partita IVA necessaria”, so this is not open to unregistered businesses or to foreign companies without Italian VAT registration.

name: Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry
Panorama Firm
best_for: Polish businesses wanting a free national directory entry.
limitations: The submission form asks whether you are the owner or a user — “Jestem: Właścicielem / Użytkownikiem” — so a third party who used a business can add it. An entry is not evidence that the named business created or approved it.

name: Firmy.net
best_for: Polish businesses wanting a free company presentation with a named, long-established operator.
limitations: Your entry does not stay on this site alone. The operator states a presentation reaches customers “z Google, aplikacji mobilnych oraz kilkunastu portali partnerskich” — from Google, mobile apps and more than a dozen partner portals. Where those entries appear is not enumerated.

name: pkt.pl
best_for: Polish businesses wanting a second national directory entry alongside Panorama Firm.
limitations: The form covers updating an existing entry, but updating data is not the same as taking ownership of a profile, so no claim flow is asserted.

name: Approved Business
best_for: UK business-to-business suppliers wanting a categorised trade listing with an enquiry form.
limitations: The free package carries a “12 month contract”. A free listing here is a term commitment, not a casual entry, and that is unusual enough to check before submitting.

name: FreeIndex
best_for: UK businesses wanting a free listing on a directory whose paid tier is priced openly rather than sold by phone.
limitations: What the email step confirms is a working email address — nothing more. It is not verification of the business, of its identity, or of the registrant’s authority to represent it, and no such verification is asserted.

name: Scoot
best_for: UK local businesses wanting one free submission that reaches a directory network rather than a single site.
limitations: Your details will be used to market to you. The form states the information “will be used to contact you by users of these directories … and suppliers (including https://web.com/en-gb ) who may wish to provide services to businesses like yours”.

name: Bizify
best_for: UK-registered businesses wanting an additional free directory listing with a named, companies-house-identified operator.
limitations: The operator contradicts its own marketing. The site promises that listings “rank” and are “built to rank too”, while the terms state: “We do not provide any warranties or guarantees as to the outcome of any of the Advertising Services, including but not limited to traffic driven to your website, orders for your goods or services, and placement of your website on any search engines.” The disclaimer is the binding text.

name: Thomson Local
best_for: UK local businesses wanting a free entry in a directory with a named, long-established operator.
limitations: The free listing EXPIRES. The operator describes it as “A three-month time limited free business listing”, so it is not a permanent presence and no permanence is asserted here.

name: Better Business Bureau
limitations: Accreditation is a paid programme, which draws recurring criticism of the rating model

name: MerchantCircle
best_for: US local businesses that find themselves already listed and want to take control of the page.
limitations: A free profile carries competitors’ advertising. The operator sells the removal of it: the paid tier promises to “Remove competitor ads from your listing” and “No ads on your page - consumers will focus only on you!”. That is a plain statement about what the free tier looks like.

name: Alignable
best_for: US small business owners who want peer referrals and local business networking rather than consumer discovery.
limitations: The cost is NOT established and is recorded as unknown. There is no pricing page, joining is presented only as “Join Today”, and the premium tier offers only “Try for Free” — a trial, which is not evidence that anything is free thereafter.
